scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me not to force my 7-year-old brother to go to bed when he woke up last night. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: My mom left me in charge, and I had a friend over. My brother is usually pretty sensitive about sleep. If he doesn't get enough, he's all over the place the next day. He's obsessed with my friends, thinks they're the coolest, and always wants to hang out. My friends find him cute and hype him up, which is why he was so excited when my friend came over. I made sure he went to bed on time, but then he woke up and came downstairs. I told him to go back to bed, but my friend suggested letting him stay. I was worried that if I tried to force him, he'd throw a fit, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. So I let him stay, and by the time the movie ended, he was almost asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him to bed around midnight. The next morning, he was cranky and didn't want to get up, even though he's not allowed to sleep past 8 on weekends. My mom found out and got mad at me. I told her that since he's 7, he should know about consequences and that staying up later would make him feel bad. I also mentioned that missing two hours of sleep isn't a big deal for a kid his age. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by not forcing him to bed. Let me think about the pros and cons. On the positive side, my brother was happy and having fun with my friend. He's sensitive, so making him go to bed might have caused a tantrum, which would have been stressful for everyone, including my friend. Plus, I carried him up later, so he still got some sleep, just not as much as usual. I also explained the consequences to my mom, thinking that he should understand that staying up late affects how he feels the next day. On the negative side, he ended up being cranky the next day, which probably made things harder for everyone. My mom was mad at me, and I might have set a precedent where he thinks he can stay up late whenever he wants. Also, even though two hours isn't a huge deal, it's still enough to affect a 7-year-old's mood and behavior. I'm also considering the long-term effects. If I let him stay up late this time, will he expect to do it again? It might be harder to enforce bedtime rules in the future. Plus, as a responsible older brother, I should be setting a good example and helping him understand the importance of sleep. Another thing to think about is how my friend influenced the situation. My friend wanted to let him stay, which might have made it harder for me to enforce the bedtime. I should have been more firm, even if it meant dealing with a tantrum, to ensure he got enough sleep. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have let him stay for a little while but set a clear time to go back to bed. That way, he wouldn't have stayed up until midnight. Or perhaps I could have given him a choice, explaining that if he stays up, he might feel tired the next day, and let him decide. But since he's 7, he might not fully grasp the consequences yet. In the end, I think not forcing him to go to bed was a mistake because it led to him being cranky the next day and upset my mom. It's important to set consistent boundaries, especially when it comes to things like sleep that affect his well-being. Even though it's tough to deal with a tantrum, it's better for his health and behavior in the long run.
